items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3821

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend chapter 704 of the laws of 1991 amending the arts and
cultural affairs law and chapter 912 of the laws of 1920 relating to
the regulation of boxing and wrestling relating to tickets to places
of entertainment, in relation to extending the provisions thereof


 PURPOSE :
The purpose of this legislation is to extend the existing ticket
resale statute.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
This bill would extend the sunset provision of Article 25 of the Arts
and Cultural Affairs Law to June 1, 2011.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In 2007, Chapters 61 and 347 created a free market for ticket resale
and repealed the enacted ticket scalping statute, in order to remove
the sunset provisions that included an alternative statute to which
the law would revert upon the sunset of currently effective law. The
law enacted in 2007 also made two significant changes to existing law;
first eliminating the premium price cap on secondary resale of
tickets; and, second, requiring that ticket resellers acquire licenses
and file bonds with the Secretary of State rather than the
commissioner of licenses for the respective political subdivision
where they would operate.

In the two years that there has been a free market for ticket resale,
there seems to be a consensus that the current system is working and
there have been very few complaints. This legislation would extend the
current law an additional two years, allowing for further examination
of the current free market for ticket resale.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3821A

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in relation to
prohibiting the agents of an operator from reselling tickets to
secondary ticket resellers; to amend chapter 704 of the laws of 1991,
amending the arts and cultural affairs law and chapter 912 of the laws
of 1920 relating to the regulation of boxing and wrestling relating to
tickets to places of entertainment, in relation to extending the
expiration of the provisions thereof; and directing the attorney
general to review and report upon the effectiveness of the regulation
of the sale of tickets to places of entertainment


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL :
The purpose of this bill is to extend the ticket resale law changes
first enacted in 2007 fifty weeks until May 15, 2010, to have a report
generated in regards to article 25 of the arts and culture law, and to
prohibit operator's agents from selling or conveying tickets to a
secondary reseller that they own or control.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section one of the bill amends and renumbers subdivision 2 of section
25.13 of the arts and cultural affairs law to section 3 and creates a
new section 2 that would prohibit any operator's agent from selling or
conveying and tickets to any secondary ticket resellers.

Section 2 amends chapter 704 of the laws of 1991, amends the arts and
cultural affairs law and chapter 912 of the laws of 1920, as amended
by chapter 374 of the laws of2007 to extend the current law from being
repealed on June 1,2009 and setting a repeal date of May 15, 2010.

Section 3 directs the attorney general to generate a report on the
effectiveness of article 25 of the arts and cultural affairs law by
February 1, 2010.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Chapter 61 of the laws of 2007 created a shift in the way that
operators, venues, ticket brokers, and the general public could access
tickets after the primary sale. Gone were the caps imposed on what
could be charged for a ticket on the secondary market in favor of a
free market approach. During the two years of free market secondary
ticket sales, few if any complaints have surfaced on the conduct of
the secondary market. What has transpired is wholesale off-loading of
tickets by a primary seller to a secondary seller without any chance
for the public to purchase tickets at first sale and the consumer
being re-directed to secondary ticket resale where both the primary
and secondary market are controlled by the same entity. This bill is
aimed at stopping that practice by prohibiting primary ticket agents
from either selling or conveying tickets to a secondary ticket seller.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that if
this act shall not have become a law on or before June 1,2009 section
two of this act shall be deemed to have been in full force and effect
on and after June 1,2009; provided, further, that the amendments to
article 25 of the arts and cultural affairs law, made by section one
of this act, shall not affect the expiration and repeal of such
article, and shall expire and be deemed repealed therewith.

BILL NUMBER:  S3821B

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in relation to
prohibiting the agents of an operator from reselling tickets to
secondary ticket resellers; to amend chapter 704 of the laws of 1991,
amending the arts and cultural affairs law and chapter 912 of the laws
of 1920 relating to the regulation of boxing and wrestling relating to
tickets to places of entertainment, in relation to extending the
expiration of the provisions thereof; and directing the secretary of
state to review and report upon the effectiveness of the regulation of
the sale of tickets to places of entertainment


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL :
The purpose of this bill is to extend the ticket resale law changes
first enacted in 2007 fifty weeks until May 15, 2010, to have a report
generated in regards to article 25 of the arts and cultural affairs

tickets to a secondary reseller that they own or control.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section one of the bill amends and renumbers subdivision 2 of section
25.13 of the arts and cultural affairs law to section 3 and creates a
new section 2 that would prohibit any operator's agent from selling or
conveying any tickets to any secondary ticket resellers. Section 3
mandates the operator or promoter to disclose whether a ticket has an
obstructed view.  Every sale or resale of such ticket shall include a
disclosure of such obstructed view.

Section 2 amends chapter 704 of the laws of 1991, amends the arts and
cultural affairs law and chapter 912 of the laws of 1920, as amended
by chapter 374 of the laws of 2007 to extend the current law from
being repealed on June 1, 2009 and setting a repeal date of May 15,
2010.

Section 3 directs the attorney general to generate a report on the
effectiveness of article 25 of the arts and cultural affairs law by
February 1, 2010.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Chapter 61 of the laws of 2007 created a shift in the way that
operators, venues, ticket brokers, and the general public could access
tickets after the primary sale. Gone were the caps imposed on what
could be charged for a ticket on the secondary market in favor of a
free market approach. During the two years of free market secondary
ticket sales, few if any complaints have surfaced on the conduct of
the secondary market. What has transpired is wholesale off-loading of
tickets by a primary seller to a secondary seller without any chance
for the public to purchase tickets at first sale and the consumer
being re-directed to secondary ticket resale where both the primary
and secondary market are controlled by the same entity. This bill is
aimed at stopping that practice by prohibiting primary ticket agents
from either selling or conveying tickets to a secondary ticket seller.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that if
this act shall not have become a law on or before June 1,2009, section
two of this act shall be deemed to have been in full force and effect
on and after June 1,2009; provided, further, that the amendments to
article 25 of the arts and cultural affairs law, made by section one
of this act, shall not affect the expiration and repeal of such
article, and shall expire and be deemed repealed therewith.

summary: Prohibits the agents of an operator from selling tickets to secondary ticket resellers; extends from June 1, 2009 until May 15, 2010, the expiration of article 25 of the arts and cultural affairs law relating to the regulation of the sales of tickets to places of entertainment; directs the attorney general to review and report upon the effectiveness of such article on or before February 1, 2010.
